image_query: Bakhshali manuscript Bodleian Library birch bark
tweets: A single dot, holding nothing, yet changing everything. In the Bakhshali manuscript, an ancient birch-bark text from the northwest Indian subcontinent, a small dot (śūnya-bindu) marks zero — among the earliest surviving uses of the symbol as a true number.

Centuries later, Brahmagupta's Brāhmasphuṭasiddhānta (628 CE) laid down the first known rules for arithmetic with zero — how it behaves in addition, subtraction, and multiplication. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history.
